sections.history: Thenthiruperai sits on the south bank of the Tamiraparani in Thoothukudi district, on the road from Tirunelveli to Tiruchendur. Vaishnava pilgrims know it for the Makara Nedunkuzhaikathar temple, one of the Nava Tirupati; its Shiva temple is the seventh of the Nava Kailasam and the shrine of Budhan, the planet Mercury. When the temple was first raised is not known, but inscriptions on its walls from the reign of the Pandya king Maravarman Sundara Pandya name the settlement Sundarapandya Chaturvedimangalam — a village granted to Vedic scholars — showing that the shrine was a living centre of worship by the thirteenth century.
sections.architecture: A compact Dravidian stone temple, it gathers the essentials of a southern Shiva shrine around a single axis: the sanctum of Kailasanathar with Nandi before it, and a separate shrine for the Goddess Azhagiya Ponnammai, whose name means "the beautiful golden mother". The Pandya inscriptions cut into its stones are themselves part of its fabric, the earliest written witness to the place's long life of worship.
sections.legends: In the Nava Kailasam story, the seventh of the lotuses set afloat on the Tamiraparani by Romasa, the disciple of Agastya, drifted to this bank, and a linga was consecrated where it stopped. Tradition holds that Budhan himself, and Varuna, the lord of the waters, worshipped Shiva here, and the place is also called Varuna Kshetram. Devotees say that worship at this shrine carries the same merit as worship at Thiruvenkadu, the great Budhan temple of the Kaveri delta. The town's name means the "southern" Tirupperai, perai being read as an old word for a fort.
sections.festivals: As the shrine of Budhan, the temple sees its devotees above all on Wednesdays, the day of Mercury, when students and those seeking clarity of speech and mind come to worship. Maha Shivaratri and the monthly pradosham are kept through the year. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Thenthiruperai is a place where the two great river circuits meet: a pilgrim can pray at the Nava Tirupati shrine of Vishnu and at the Nava Kailasam shrine of Shiva in the same short walk. Many come with a single prayer — to Budhan, for a clear mind and a ready tongue — and students are often among them.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Wednesdays are busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Men are traditionally asked to remove the upper garment before the sanctum, as at many southern shrines; follow the posted rules.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thenthiruperai lies in Thoothukudi district on the Tirunelveli–Tiruchendur road, about 38 km from Tirunelveli; buses on that route stop in the town. The nearest railway station is Alwarthirunagari on the Tirunelveli–Tiruchendur line, and the nearest airport is Thoothukudi. The Kailasanathar temple is separate from the Makara Nedunkuzhaikathar Vishnu temple in the same town.
